title: Trading Multiples and Peer Selection Mastery
description: Practice selecting peer groups, interpreting trading multiples, and making relative valuation judgments under realistic conditions.

interactions.prompt: You're valuing a mid-cap SaaS company. Peer set medians: EV/Revenue 8.2x, EV/EBITDA 32x. Your target trades at EV/Revenue 6.1x and EV/EBITDA 35x. What's the key signal?

options.text: Target is undervalued on all metrics
Target has lower revenue growth but worse margins than peers
Target appears cheap on revenue but has lower margins than peers
Target's EBITDA multiple is irrelevant for SaaS

interactions.prompt: When selecting comparable companies, the most critical screening criteria are ____, business model, and end-market exposure.

options.text: Stock price level
Revenue growth and profitability profile
Headquarters location
Number of employees

interactions.prompt: You're building a comp set for Chipotle. You can only include 5 companies. Do you prioritize restaurant chains with similar growth rates or similar market caps?

options.text: Similar growth rates—growth is the primary multiple driver
Similar market caps—size drives liquidity and investor base
Equal weight to both—neither dominates
Neither—focus only on same cuisine type

interactions.prompt: Peer group P/E multiples: CrowdStrike 62x, Palo Alto 48x, Fortinet 40x, SentinelOne NM (negative earnings). Median P/E is 48x. What should concern you most?

options.text: The median is too high to be useful
Excluding SentinelOne biases the median upward
NM exclusion shrinks the sample and may skew the benchmark
P/E is always the best multiple for cybersecurity

interactions.prompt: Rank these multiples from most to least appropriate for valuing a high-growth, unprofitable e-commerce company like Coupang.

options.text: P/E ratio
EV/Revenue
EV/Gross Profit
Price/Book Value

interactions.prompt: Your comp set for a U.S. specialty retailer includes one outlier trading at 25x EV/EBITDA vs. a group median of 12x due to a rumored acquisition. Do you include or exclude it?

options.text: Exclude it—M&A speculation distorts the trading multiple
Include it—removing data points reduces sample integrity
Include but use median, which naturally limits outlier impact
Replace it with the industry average multiple

interactions.prompt: You're presenting a comp analysis to a skeptical board. Rank these steps by importance for building credibility in your valuation.

options.text: Show a wide range of multiples from many sectors
Clearly justify each peer's inclusion with business rationale
Normalize financials for one-time items across all comps
Present both mean and median with dispersion context

interactions.prompt: Your target's largest comp just announced it's pivoting from hardware to a subscription model. Its forward EV/Revenue jumped from 3x to 9x overnight. How should you adjust your analysis?

options.text: Remove the comp entirely—its business model no longer matches
Keep it but use its pre-announcement multiple
Keep it with the new multiple since markets are efficient
Reclassify it as a SaaS comp and flag the divergence

interactions.priorContext: Previously your comp set was stable with 6 hardware peers all trading at 2.5x-4x EV/Revenue. Now one peer's pivot has fundamentally changed its valuation profile, disrupting your benchmark.
